sentenceText: The concept of Virtual Reality (VR) dates back to sci-fi stories of the 1930s, but the second half of the 20th century saw video game designers bring these fictional technologies to life.
In the 1990s, Sega designed motion-tracking gaming headsets, but they never took off.
Interest in VR was later regained in the 2010s when Oculus VR launched the visually realistic Oculus Rift headset, and VR has become more advanced and widely available ever since.
Combined with equipment such as headsets and sensory-fitted gloves, VR allows you to cooperate with simulated（模拟）landscapes and sets.
For instance, simulated surgeries can prepare surgeons for operations, while the distraction of another world can reduce a patient’s pain-related brain activity.
Augmented（增强的）Reality(AR) also offers another version of reality, but there are key differences.
Its portable, accessible equipment, such as smartphones or tablets, means it’s more broadly used.
For instance, you can travel in an unfamiliar city by using AR walking directions through your phone.
Both AR and VR are industries set to boom and change reality as we know it.
